issues.legal_issue: A first appellate court deciding a specific-performance suit cannot decree relief solely because it finds the agreement genuine without considering other material aspects, including readiness and willingness.
material_facts: The trial court dismissed the specific-performance suit after answering the issues against the plaintiffs.
The High Court reversed the dismissal and decreed specific performance principally on its finding that the agreement was genuine.
The High Court did not consider other material aspects of the suit, including readiness and willingness.
The Supreme Court set aside the High Court judgment and remitted the first appeal for fresh hearing, without expressing an opinion on the merits.
issues.conclusion: The High Court judgment was set aside and the first appeal was remitted for fresh hearing so that all available contentions and relevant aspects, including readiness and willingness, could be considered.
issues.legal_principle: In a specific-performance suit, a finding that the agreement is genuine is not by itself sufficient to decree relief; the court must also consider other relevant aspects, including readiness and willingness. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this principle.

predicates.specific_performance_appeal: The matter was an appeal from a first appellate judgment in a specific-performance suit.
predicates.appellate_court_decreed_relief_on_docume: The appellate court decreed relief principally because it found the agreement genuine.
predicates.readiness_willingness_not_considered: The appellate court did not consider whether the claimant was ready and willing to perform or other material aspects of the suit.

issues.definition: When an appeal in a specific-performance suit involves a decree based principally on document authenticity without consideration of readiness and willingness, the first appellate judgment is set aside and the case is remitted for fresh hearing.
